note: Register of outward-facing claims. Verified claims are re-computed by 'python -m audit claims --verify'; any drift fails CI. Unverified and retired claims are never promoted to facts. Denominators and boundaries are mandatory because this repository's subject is honest uncertainty.

claims.statement: The default controlled experiment publishes exactly six evidence files, listed in manifest.json.
claims.boundary: Default --seeds 6 controlled experiment only; not a specification for production bundles. Full as-of inputs live in views.jsonl, keyed by input_sha256.

claims.statement: At the 0.7 checkpoint the rules-v2 strict replay policy yields 6 true stops, 0 false stops and 1 abstention; readiness is blocked.
claims.denominator: 18 controlled trials (6 pass / 12 fail); fail_recall uses all 12 failed runs including abstentions
claims.boundary: A single 4x4 grid toy scene; all 12 failures are controlled fault injections, not natural failures. This demonstrates a workflow, not production early-stop effectiveness or compute savings.

claims.statement: The two rule profiles are defined once in rl_risk_replay/policy.py under distinct machine-readable IDs.
claims.boundary: Behaviour is intentionally unchanged from v0.2. This resolves the rules-v2 naming ambiguity; it is not a validation of either policy's effectiveness.

claims.statement: main pins exactly 142 archived v1 artifacts in data/manifest.json as a content-addressed provenance anchor.
claims.denominator: length of manifest.files; bodies are verified separately by 'python -m audit data --root <archive/v1 checkout>' in CI
claims.boundary: A hash anchor only. It does not make the archived CSVs usable for strict replay: they have no available_at field, and strict-replay-eligible historical runs remain 0. It says nothing about producer authenticity or effect validity.

claims.statement: 18 observed runs (6 pass / 12 fail) plus 48 legacy/offline runs are referenced by the frozen v0.2 research note.
claims.denominator: Recorded figure from a historical Go2W data snapshot; the 142 artifact bodies are archived on archive/v1 and hash-pinned in data/manifest.json, but the cohort statistic itself is not recomputed
claims.boundary: One trainer only; all 12 observed failures are zero-S0 controlled ablations; legacy CSV has no available_at timestamp and cannot enter strict replay.
claims.blocker: Not reproducible from this repository with a stdlib command: requires the external Go2W dataset and the DuckDB research layer over an archive/v1 checkout. Do not cite as a validated effect.

claims.statement: saved_yuan_compute estimated monetary compute savings from early stopping.
claims.denominator: v1 estimation formula, not a measurement
claims.boundary: The project never claimed realized compute savings; no auditable cost baseline exists.
claims.blocker: Retired together with the original prediction goal. See docs/adr/0001-from-prediction-to-evidence.md.

claims.statement: The sentinel agent raises exactly one producer-silence alert for a run whose last metrics looked healthy and whose writer then went silent, without any finish event; a resumed event resets the incident, and a finished run never alerts.
claims.denominator: 1 hung demo run under a virtual clock; the alert rule is data-availability based, not metric based
claims.boundary: Deterministic self-test on synthetic events; not a tuned production hang detector. Recommendation-only: alerts notify a human, no training process is touched.

claims.statement: Without any schema change, the agent derives resume lineage from (task, seed): a retry after a cancelled attempt is reported as attempt 2, with the cancelled run's last observed step counted as lost compute.
claims.denominator: 1 cancelled run + 1 retry under a virtual clock; steps_lost sums each cancelled run's last observed step, a floor on wasted compute rather than an exact measure
claims.boundary: Lineage is an agent-side derived view keyed on (task, seed); independent reruns of the same (task, seed) are also counted as attempts. SIGKILL cannot be intercepted by any handler; the producer-silence alert is the net for that case.

claims.statement: The SB3 adapter streams contract-valid events from a real PPO run (CartPole-v1); a real SIGTERM during training becomes a cancelled finish whose last step is counted as lost compute; a retry is reported as attempt 2 with resumed_after_cancelled.
claims.denominator: 2 real runs on 2026-11-06 (Apple M5, Python 3.12.14, torch 2.15.0, stable-baselines3 2.9.2, gymnasium 1.4.0): attempt 1 interrupted by SIGTERM at 358,145 steps, attempt 2 completed 40,705 steps; 1,548 events ingested by the agent with 0 contract rejections
claims.boundary: Local reproduction only: torch and stable-baselines3 are deliberately not CI dependencies, so these numbers are not recomputable from this repository. SB3's logger clears on every dump, so sample metrics arrive in bursts; rollout/ep_rew_mean capture is timing-dependent and the observed samples carry train/* metrics. The adapter was additionally exercised via stub tests that remain CI-gated.
claims.blocker: Not CI-reproducible without installing torch/SB3 in CI. Reproduce locally with scripts/sb3_real_demo.py against any running agent (POST the event files to /events); output depends on wall-clock timing.
